what: Validation of the DESIGNED organism (the "winged zebrafish") against the REAL flying fish (Exocoetidae), genetically and phenotypically.

prereg.note: hashed before the first number was produced

organisms.reference_real: flying fishes, Exocoetidae (49 museum specimens, Daane 2021 Data S1A; Park and Choi 2010 specimen L3 for aerodynamics)
organisms.baseline: zebrafish, Danio rerio (adult at 365 d: SL 0.04426 m, mass 0.001058 kg, development/zebrafish/trajectory.mjs)
organisms.design: the "winged zebrafish": germline trans-heterozygote lat4a nr21/+ (ZFIN slc43a2a, allele dmh26, T200K) with kcnh2a lof/+ (the longfin dt2 chromosome-2 inversion). genotype/compare-2x2.json panel B.
organisms.design_has_a_real_counterpart: YES: Daane et al. 2021 built exactly this double heterozygote and state it phenocopies flying-fish fin proportions. Its measurements are figure-only.

part1_phenotypic.formula: f = (D - Z) / (F - Z); residual r = F - D; INSIDE iff min(F_obs) <= D <= max(F_obs)

per_axis.note: TWO independent reasons, on opposite sides: the baseline has no value and the design has only a figure. This is the axis the whole design claim is about.

flyingfish.reason: Daane 2021 Data S1A sheet A measures pectoral and pelvic fins only; there is no caudal column, and no other fetched source gives flying-fish caudal fin length / SL

cannot_score_reason_tally.note: an axis can carry more than one reason, so these do not sum to 9

part1_phenotypic.verdict: NOT CLOSE, and largely UNSHOWN. 9 of 10 axes cannot be scored. The single scoreable axis scores FAIL at f = 0.00. The axis the entire design claim rests on (pectoral fin length / SL) cannot be scored, and for two independent reasons at once.

prereg_trigger_check.deviation: See RUNS.md deviation 1. The letter of the pre-registered rule would award "close" by default here, because none of the three FAIL triggers can fire at n_scored = 1. That reading is refused: the only scored axis is a FAIL, and the result is reported as NOT CLOSE.

G - conv. aa subst..note: one row has no gene name (ENSXMAG00000017216, "NA") and is excluded from the locus count

K - accel CNEs Exocoet..note: GAP: this sheet is a GO-term enrichment table (GO ID, GO Name, # CNEs, q-value), NOT a list of elements or of genes. The 131425 sum of its "# CNEs" column counts each CNE once per GO term it maps to, so it is neither an element count nor a locus count, and it is not used.

M - accel CNEs halfbeak.note: the same GAP as sheet K; the sum 126463 is likewise unusable. This sheet is also halfbeak, not Exocoetidae.

J - Exocoeidae phylop.note: SUPPORTING only; pre-registered as NOT part of the denominator

a_loci_known_to_differ.formula: |distinct Ensembl loci in sheet G UNION sheet I|
a_loci_known_to_differ.context: 74 loci against the 23,611 predicted protein-coding genes of the Hirundichthys speculiger assembly (Xu et al. 2021, fetched in this thread) = 0.31 % of the gene set. The 74 is what is KNOWN to differ, not what differs.

members.evidence: sheet G row 2: lat4a, F326L, ticked for E. viridis, O. micropterus AND Exocoetidae, and ticked in the fin-screens column. Also sheet J row 6 as slc43a2a, accelerated, phyloP p = 8.37e-3. The same Ensembl ID carries both names, so lat4a and slc43a2a are one locus.

misses.searched: every one of the 14 sheets of Data S1, for kcnh2, lat4, slc43a2, prrx1, longfin, dt2 and nr21
misses.only_kcnh2_hit_anywhere: kcnh2b (ENSORLG00000004137) in sheet H "fin and limb genes", which is a candidate list and not one of the sheets that record what differs in flying fishes
misses.classification: NEAR MISS (a paralogue, in a different sheet); does not count toward B

near_misses_for_lat4a.classification: NEAR MISS: the glider RER signal and the strongest phyloP acceleration (p = 1e-5) sit on the b PARALOGUE, not on the a copy the design edits

c_fraction_reproduced.reading: the design reproduces 1.4 % of the loci known to differ in flying fishes: a real, named hit on one convergent locus, and negligible as a fraction.

d_design_changes_not_known_to_differ.note: half of the design is a locus with no flying-fish evidence at all. It was chosen because it overgrows fins in zebrafish, not because flying fishes changed it.

weaker_claim_preregistered.meaning: the design does hit a genuine convergent flying-fish locus. This is the claim the design wins, and it is the one that was pre-registered as winnable.

part2_genetic.verdict: C = 0.0135, the TOKEN band: not the pre-registered FAIL (C < 0.01), and not substantial. A hit on the right locus and a miss on the genome.

posthoc_sensitivity.label: POST-HOC (exploratory); not pre-registered, and not in the headline

with_sheet_J_added.note: adding the phyloP sheet to the denominator moves C below 0.01, into the pre-registered "negligible" band. The pre-registered answer stands; this is reported because the choice of denominator changes the band, and a reader is entitled to know that.

part3_lean_gate.gate_rule: PASSES = no violated and no cannot-evaluate; FAILS = any violated; UNDECIDED = no violated but some cannot-evaluate. UNDECIDED IS NOT A PASS.

design_violations.needed: an implied mass exponent within 3 +/- 0.1 against the reference specimen
design_violations.honest_qualification: the REAL fish is cannot-evaluate on this row only because it IS the reference specimen (lengthRatio = 1), so the row cannot test the animal it is calibrated on. The violation is real, but its content is a BODY-SIZE mismatch: a 4.4 cm, 1.06 g zebrafish against a 20.3 cm, 60 g flying fish.
the same single underlying fact as C7b, not a second independent failure. Empirical band: a reader may reject the observation it rests on.

real_violations.note: the REAL flying fish fails this row: level flight at 10 m/s needs 29 times its aerobic ceiling. This is the known and expected result (flying fishes glide, they do not fly), and it is exactly why a design that "passes" a row the real animal fails must be treated as suspicious rather than as better.

undecided_where_real_decided.note: the minimum-speed bound, the single most relevant constraint for a flier, cannot be evaluated on the design, because the design has no fin area, no lift coefficient and no airspeed.
a provenance row: it can say a design is outside everything measured, never that it is ruled out. The design cannot even reach that, having no fin ratio at all.

how_much_of_the_design_lean_tests.method: the pre-registered one-at-a-time ablation: drop each supplied input, record which row ids change verdict
how_much_of_the_design_lean_tests.verdict: THE GATE IS WEAK. All 3 supplied inputs move a verdict, but only 3 of 21 rows are decided, and the two body inputs move the same single pair of rows (C7b and E2 are one fact). Lean is testing the design on body size, and on whether one amino-acid change is reachable in one nucleotide substitution. It is testing nothing aerodynamic, nothing developmental and nothing about the fins, which is the entire point of the design.

control_posthoc.label: POST-HOC (exploratory); not pre-registered
control_posthoc.arm: the REAL flying fish given only the inputs the design has (SL, mass, and the same genotype edits)
control_posthoc.reading: matched to the design inputs, the real animal is UNDECIDED, not FAILS: it does not trip C7b or E2, because it is the reference. So the two design violations are produced by the design being a different size from the reference, and the comparison is not input-matched. This weakens the design-only label without removing it.

part4_the_real_experiment.what_daanes_double_heterozygote_achieved: in the authors own words, from genotype/compare-2x2.json panel B

quotes.quote: Interestingly, double mutants between kcnh2alof/+ and lat4anr21/+ are viable and show specific, non-additive variation in proportion among fins: while all fins of kcnh2alof/+ are overgrown and all fins of lat4anr21/+ are shortened, the lat4anr21/+;kcnh2alof/+ fish show wild-type-sized medial fins, while the paired fins are overgrown (Figure 4).
Surprisingly, the caudal fin of kcnh2alof/+;lat4anr21/+, while generally wild type in size, is hypocercal, with an elongated ventral lobe.
The nr21 mutant, however, does not have a statistically decreased body size (Figure 3B).

The overall fin phenotype of the kcnh2alof;lat4anr21 fish is thus remarkably similar to that of flying fishes, suggesting the interaction between these two genes is sufficient to phenocopy this key innovation and organismal bauplan of flying fishes (Figure 4).

its_own_limits: the numbers are FIGURE-ONLY: Figure 4B pectoral fin length, Figure 4C caudal fin length, Figures S2A and S2B lepidotrichial segments. No numeric value appears in the text, the legends, or the fourteen sheets of Data S1.
segmentation is regular, unlike the kcnk5b overgrowth mutant: a quality claim, not a measurement
the overlap with flying fishes is at lat4a only, and the convergent flying-fish substitution is F326L while the zebrafish allele is T200K: a DIFFERENT residue in the same gene
the glider RER signal and the strongest phyloP acceleration are on slc43a2b, the paralogue, not on the slc43a2a the allele sits in
part4_the_real_experiment.does_the_real_experiment_already_achieve: YES, ENTIRELY. The design IS Daanes double heterozygote. Every phenotypic claim the design makes is a claim about an animal that Daane et al. already built, scored and published in 2021, and the authors had already stated that it phenocopies the flying-fish bauplan. That is a result about their experiment, not about us. Our contribution here is the validation arithmetic, not the organism.

joint_result.preregistered_consequence: PREREG rule 1: far AND fails means drop the claim outright.
but_read_this_with_the_qualifications: the two design violations are one fact (body size against a single reference specimen), and the real animal is untestable on those rows by construction
the real flying fish ALSO FAILS the gate (E3, by a factor of 29), so "FAILS" does not separate the design from the target
18 of 21 rows are cannot-evaluate on the design, so the gate is weak and its FAILS verdict carries little information either way
Part 1 is better described as UNSHOWN than as far: the measurement that would settle it sits in a figure we refused to digitise
joint_result.what_actually_follows: The claim that we can DESIGN an organism is not supported by this validation, and the reason is not that the design scored badly: it is that the design is not measurable on the axes that define it, and the one genetic number that can be computed (1/74) says the design reproduces a single convergent locus out of everything known to differ. Dropping the claim outright under rule 1 overstates what this gate can tell us; the honest position is PREREG rule 2, drop the claim as UNSUPPORTED.
